title: Excess Return
body:
**Excess return** is the return above the [[Risk-Free Rate]]:

$$
R_p - R_f
$$

It is the numerator of the [[Sharpe Ratio]], and it answers what the risk actually bought.
A strategy returning 5% in a period when a government bond returned 4% produced 1% of excess
return, and that 1% is what the volatility was accepted for.

The concept is what separates a good investment from a rising market. During a period when
everything rose, a portfolio that rose is unremarkable, and the question is whether it rose
more than the alternative that carried no risk.

Excess return can be negative, which is the informative case: a strategy that made money and
underperformed the risk-free rate lost money in the only sense that matters here.
